products.title: The Meath Larder
products.descriptionHtml:
A food hamper built entirely from producers within an hour of our door in Dunshaughlin.

Kilbeg Dairy make their cheddar three miles from us. Sheridans have been selling cheese in Meath since 1995. Killowen Farm in Wexford make the chutney in small batches from their own apples. We buy from all of them directly, and we pack the boxes ourselves.

Everything arrives in a deep kraft box, wrapped in tissue and hand tied with ribbon, with your message written on a card inside the lid.

products.title: The Big Thank You
products.descriptionHtml:
For the neighbour who fed the cat for a fortnight.

A bottle of red, a full cheeseboard set and chocolate. Enough that the thank you is obvious without anybody being embarrassed by it.

A deep kraft box with the bottle upright, everything else packed around it, hand tied.

images.alt: The Big Thank You: a bottle of red wine beside a box of Butlers chocolates, arranged in a green Parcel Concierge gift box
Close view of a bottle of red wine beside a box of Butlers chocolates
The green gift box The Big Thank You arrives in, with the contents packed in wood wool
The Big Thank You photographed square on

hamper.packaging: A deep kraft box with the bottle upright, everything else packed around it, hand tied.

products.title: Domaine Bellefont Chablis Premier Cru
products.descriptionHtml:
Sharp green apple and lemon, with a chalky edge that makes your mouth water. Dry, and not remotely sweet.

Made by a family domaine in Chablis, northern Burgundy, on the limestone that gives the wine its bite.

Drink it with oysters, smoked salmon or a roast chicken.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Domaine Bellefont Chablis Premier Cru standing against a plain background
Domaine Bellefont Chablis Premier Cru label in close up

products.title: Bodegas Aldea Rioja Reserva
products.descriptionHtml:
Soft red fruit and vanilla from three years in oak, with enough grip to stand up to a steak.

From a family bodega in Rioja Alta who have been bottling their own since the 1950s.

Steak, lamb, or a hard sheep cheese.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Bodegas Aldea Rioja Reserva standing against a plain background
Bodegas Aldea Rioja Reserva label in close up

products.title: Quinta do Ribeiro Douro Tinto
products.descriptionHtml:
Dark plum and blackberry with a warm, dry finish. Big, but not heavy going.

Grown on terraces above the Douro in northern Portugal, on the same vines that go into port.

Stew, roast beef, or anything off a barbecue.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Quinta do Ribeiro Douro Tinto standing against a plain background
Quinta do Ribeiro Douro Tinto label in close up

products.title: Finca del Sol Malbec
products.descriptionHtml:
Ripe blackcurrant and a hint of cocoa, smooth all the way through. An easy bottle to open on a Tuesday.

Grown high in the Uco Valley in Mendoza, where the cold nights keep the fruit fresh.

Burgers, hard cheese, or on its own.

images.alt: Bottle of Finca del Sol Malbec standing against a plain background
Finca del Sol Malbec label in close up

products.title: Pazo de Miño Albariño
products.descriptionHtml:
Peach and lime with a salty finish, the way white wine tastes near the sea.

From Rías Baixas on the Atlantic coast of Galicia, a few miles inland from the water.

Prawns, crab, or a plate of ham.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Pazo de Miño Albariño standing against a plain background
Pazo de Miño Albariño label in close up

products.title: Maison Vireau Champagne Brut
products.descriptionHtml:
Fine bubbles, green apple and toast. Dry, but round enough to drink on its own.

A grower Champagne from the Marne valley, made by the family who farm the vines rather than a large house.

Drink it before dinner, or with anything fried.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Maison Vireau Champagne Brut standing against a plain background
Maison Vireau Champagne Brut label in close up

products.title: Ca del Ponte Prosecco Superiore
products.descriptionHtml:
Pear and white flowers, soft bubbles, off dry. Easier going than Champagne and meant to be.

From a single estate in Valdobbiadene rather than a co-op, which is why it tastes of something.

Aperitif, brunch, or with a slice of cake.

images.alt: Bottle of Ca del Ponte Prosecco Superiore standing against a plain background
Ca del Ponte Prosecco Superiore label in close up

products.title: Château Lansac Rosé
products.descriptionHtml:
Pale, dry, strawberry and pink grapefruit. Cold, in a garden, in July.

Made in Provence, on the same estate that has been growing these grapes since the 1970s.

Salad, grilled fish, or nothing at all.

images.alt: Bottle of Château Lansac Rosé standing against a plain background
Château Lansac Rosé label in close up

products.title: Graham Estate Late Bottled Vintage Port
products.descriptionHtml:
Sweet, thick and dark, with figs, chocolate and a long finish. A small glass goes a long way.

From the Douro in northern Portugal, aged in cask for four years before bottling.

Blue cheese, dark chocolate, or on its own after dinner.

images.alt: Bottle of Graham Estate Late Bottled Vintage Port standing against a plain background
Graham Estate Late Bottled Vintage Port label in close up

products.title: Barone Ferri Barolo
products.descriptionHtml:
Rose, tar and sour cherry, with firm tannin. It needs an hour open, and it is worth the hour.

From Piedmont in north west Italy, from a grower with four hectares and no second label.

Braised beef, mushroom risotto, aged cheese.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Barone Ferri Barolo standing against a plain background
Barone Ferri Barolo label in close up

products.title: Clos Saint Aubin Sauternes
products.descriptionHtml:
Honey, apricot and marmalade, sweet but not cloying because the acidity holds it up.

From Sauternes in Bordeaux, where the autumn mist does the work that makes this wine possible.

Blue cheese, tart, or foie gras.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Clos Saint Aubin Sauternes standing against a plain background
Clos Saint Aubin Sauternes label in close up

products.title: Château Verdier Châteauneuf du Pape
products.descriptionHtml:
Warm, spicy and full, with dried herbs and dark fruit. Tastes like the south of France in a glass.

Grown on the stony ground north of Avignon, where the pebbles hold the heat overnight.

Lamb, game, or a hard mountain cheese.

images.alt: Bottle of Château Verdier Châteauneuf du Pape standing against a plain background
Château Verdier Châteauneuf du Pape label in close up

wine.tastingNote: Dried herbs, dark fruit, black pepper.

products.title: Slane Bridge Single Pot Still Irish Whiskey
products.descriptionHtml:
Thick and oily, with baked apple, clove and a long warm finish. Water opens it up.

Distilled and bottled in Ireland from malted and unmalted barley, aged in bourbon and sherry casks.

Neat, with a drop of water, after dinner.

images.alt: Bottle of Slane Bridge Single Pot Still Irish Whiskey standing against a plain background
Slane Bridge Single Pot Still Irish Whiskey label in close up

products.title: Slane Bridge Single Cask Reserve
products.descriptionHtml:
Heavier than the standard bottling, with dried fig, orange peel and a lot of sherry cask behind it.

One cask, one bottling run, numbered by hand. When the cask is gone it is gone.

Neat. Nothing else needed.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Slane Bridge Single Cask Reserve standing against a plain background
Slane Bridge Single Cask Reserve label in close up

products.title: Tara Hill Small Batch Gin
products.descriptionHtml:
Juniper first, then gorse, elderflower and a green herbal finish. Works with tonic and works in a martini.

Distilled in Meath in batches of four hundred bottles, using botanicals picked within the county.

Tonic and a slice of grapefruit.

images.alt: Bottle of Tara Hill Small Batch Gin standing against a plain background
Tara Hill Small Batch Gin label in close up

products.title: Tara Hill Coastal Vodka
products.descriptionHtml:
Clean and slightly sweet, with a soft finish. Made from Irish grain and filtered through charcoal.

Distilled in Meath by the same small team who make the gin.

Neat and very cold, or with soda and lime.

images.alt: Bottle of Tara Hill Coastal Vodka standing against a plain background
Tara Hill Coastal Vodka label in close up

products.title: Boyne Coffee Liqueur
products.descriptionHtml:
Strong coffee, brown sugar and a bitter edge that keeps it from being a dessert.

Made in Meath with coffee roasted twenty minutes from the distillery.

Over ice, in an espresso martini, or on ice cream.

images.alt: Bottle of Boyne Coffee Liqueur standing against a plain background
Boyne Coffee Liqueur label in close up

products.title: Weingut Fassler Riesling Trocken
products.descriptionHtml:
Lime, green apple and a wet slate edge. Bone dry, despite what people expect of Riesling.

From the Mosel in Germany, grown on slate so steep the fruit is picked by hand.

Thai food, pork, or anything with chilli in it.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Weingut Fassler Riesling Trocken standing against a plain background
Weingut Fassler Riesling Trocken label in close up

products.title: Cave de Roussel Picpoul de Pinet
products.descriptionHtml:
Sharp, lemony and light, with a salty finish. The house white that never disappoints.

From the Languedoc coast in southern France, beside the oyster beds it is made for.

Shellfish, goat cheese, or a hot afternoon.

images.alt: Bottle of Cave de Roussel Picpoul de Pinet standing against a plain background
Cave de Roussel Picpoul de Pinet label in close up

products.title: Tenuta Marchesi Pinot Grigio
products.descriptionHtml:
Pear and almond, soft and dry. Easy going without being boring, which is rarer than it sounds.

Grown in Friuli in north east Italy, where Pinot Grigio actually comes from.

Pasta, salads, or on its own before dinner.

images.alt: Bottle of Tenuta Marchesi Pinot Grigio standing against a plain background
Tenuta Marchesi Pinot Grigio label in close up

products.title: Mas de la Garrigue Rosé
products.descriptionHtml:
Redcurrant and peach, dry and pale, with more grip than most rosé.

From the Rhône, made from Grenache picked early so it keeps its acidity.

Grilled fish, charcuterie, tomatoes.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Mas de la Garrigue Rosé standing against a plain background
Mas de la Garrigue Rosé label in close up

products.title: Quinta Rosada Rosé
products.descriptionHtml:
Strawberry and watermelon, off dry and very easy. A crowd rosé rather than a thinking one.

From the Alentejo in southern Portugal, made to be drunk cold and young.

Barbecue, salad, or a garden.

images.alt: Bottle of Quinta Rosada Rosé standing against a plain background
Quinta Rosada Rosé label in close up

products.title: Bodega Aldea Rosado
products.descriptionHtml:
Raspberry and orange peel, dry, with a bit of weight to it. Rosé that works in October.

From the same Rioja Alta bodega as our Reserva, made from Garnacha.

Roast chicken, paella, hard cheese.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Bodega Aldea Rosado standing against a plain background
Bodega Aldea Rosado label in close up

products.title: Maison Vireau Blanc de Blancs
products.descriptionHtml:
All Chardonnay, so it is finer and sharper than the standard bottling. Lemon, chalk and toast.

From the same grower family in the Marne valley, from their oldest Chardonnay parcel.

Oysters, or on its own at the start of an evening.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Maison Vireau Blanc de Blancs standing against a plain background
Maison Vireau Blanc de Blancs label in close up

products.title: Casa Bruna Cava Brut Nature
products.descriptionHtml:
Bone dry with no added sugar at all, so it tastes of apple and bread rather than sweetness.

Made near Barcelona by the traditional method, aged on its lees for two years.

Aperitif, tapas, fried fish.

images.alt: Bottle of Casa Bruna Cava Brut Nature standing against a plain background
Casa Bruna Cava Brut Nature label in close up

products.title: Graham Estate Tawny Port, 10 Year
products.descriptionHtml:
Caramel, walnut and dried apricot. Lighter and nuttier than a vintage port, and it keeps once opened.

Aged ten years in cask in the Douro before bottling, which is where the nuttiness comes from.

Cheese, nuts, or a cold night.

images.alt: Bottle of Graham Estate Tawny Port, 10 Year standing against a plain background
Graham Estate Tawny Port, 10 Year label in close up

products.title: Bodega del Sur Pedro Ximénez
products.descriptionHtml:
Almost black, thick as syrup, all raisin and molasses. Pour it over ice cream and watch what happens.

From Andalusia, made from grapes dried in the sun before pressing.

Vanilla ice cream, blue cheese, or a very small glass on its own.

images.alt: Bottle of Bodega del Sur Pedro Ximénez standing against a plain background
Bodega del Sur Pedro Ximénez label in close up

products.title: Hill of Tara Single Malt
products.descriptionHtml:
Lighter than our pot still, with pear, vanilla and a soft finish. A good first single malt.

Distilled in Ireland from malted barley and aged eight years in bourbon casks.

Neat, or with one ice cube.

images.alt: Bottle of Hill of Tara Single Malt standing against a plain background
Hill of Tara Single Malt label in close up

products.title: Slane Bridge Cask Strength
products.descriptionHtml:
Undiluted, so it is hot until you add water, then it opens into honey, orange and clove.

Bottled straight from the cask with nothing added, at whatever strength the cask gave.

Neat with a few drops of water.

images.alt: Bottle of Slane Bridge Cask Strength standing against a plain background
Slane Bridge Cask Strength label in close up

products.title: Tara Hill Sloe Gin
products.descriptionHtml:
Deep red, tart and sweet at once, with almond behind the fruit. Not a syrup.

Made in Meath from sloes picked in the hedgerows after the first frost.

Neat after a walk, or topped with sparkling wine.

images.alt: Bottle of Tara Hill Sloe Gin standing against a plain background
Tara Hill Sloe Gin label in close up

products.title: Rioja Reserva and Glasses Set
products.descriptionHtml:
Our Rioja Reserva, soft red fruit and vanilla from three years in oak, with two crystal glasses.

The wine is from a family bodega in Rioja Alta we import directly. The glasses are cut crystal.

Steak, lamb, or a hard sheep cheese.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Rioja Reserva and Glasses Set standing against a plain background
Rioja Reserva and Glasses Set label in close up

products.title: Champagne and Flutes Set
products.descriptionHtml:
Grower Champagne with fine bubbles and a toasty edge, boxed with two crystal flutes.

Made by the family who farm the vines in the Marne valley, not by a large house.

Anything that counts as an occasion.

We import this one ourselves. No other retailer in Ireland stocks it.

images.alt: Bottle of Champagne and Flutes Set standing against a plain background
Champagne and Flutes Set label in close up

products.title: Whiskey and Tumblers Set
products.descriptionHtml:
Single pot still Irish whiskey, thick and oily with baked apple and clove, and two cut crystal tumblers.

Distilled and bottled in Ireland, aged in bourbon and sherry casks.

Neat, with a drop of water, after dinner.

images.alt: Bottle of Whiskey and Tumblers Set standing against a plain background
Whiskey and Tumblers Set label in close up

products.title: Port and Cheese Knife Set
products.descriptionHtml:
Ten year tawny port, caramel and walnut, with a pair of cheese knives that will outlast the bottle.

The port is aged ten years in cask in the Douro. The knives are stainless with ash handles.

A blue cheese and an hour with nothing else to do.

images.alt: Bottle of Port and Cheese Knife Set standing against a plain background
Port and Cheese Knife Set label in close up

products.title: Wild Gorse Soy Candle
products.descriptionHtml: Poured in Ireland in soy wax, scented with gorse and sea air. Burns for around forty hours. Add it to a hamper and it fills the top of the box.

images.alt: Wild Gorse Soy Candle photographed on a plain background

products.title: Sea Air Reed Diffuser
products.descriptionHtml: A hundred millilitres of oil and eight reeds, which lasts about three months in a hallway. Made in Ireland. It goes well in a pamper hamper.

images.alt: Sea Air Reed Diffuser photographed on a plain background

products.title: Skelligs Sea Salt Chocolate Bar
products.descriptionHtml: Dark chocolate with sea salt, made in Kerry on the Ring of Kerry road. Ninety grams. The obvious thing to add to any food hamper.

images.alt: Skelligs Sea Salt Chocolate Bar photographed on a plain background

products.title: Bean and Goose Praline Selection
products.descriptionHtml: Twelve pralines made in Wexford in small batches. Contains nuts and milk. Add it to a hamper or send it with a card.

images.alt: Bean and Goose Praline Selection photographed on a plain background

products.title: Handmade Shortbread Tin
products.descriptionHtml: All butter shortbread in a tin that gets reused. Two hundred grams. It goes with the tea in a sympathy box and with the coffee in a breakfast one.

images.alt: Handmade Shortbread Tin photographed on a plain background

products.title: Cut Crystal Tumbler Pair
products.descriptionHtml: Two hand cut crystal tumblers, weighted at the base. They are the glasses in our whiskey hampers, sold separately for anyone who already has the bottle.

images.alt: Cut Crystal Tumbler Pair photographed on a plain background

products.title: Crystal Wine Glass Pair
products.descriptionHtml: Two crystal wine glasses with a fine rim. Dishwasher safe, which is unusual at this weight. Add them to any wine hamper.

images.alt: Crystal Wine Glass Pair photographed on a plain background

products.title: Irish Ash Serving Board
products.descriptionHtml: Turned from Irish ash in Wicklow and finished with food safe oil. Thirty five centimetres across. It goes under the cheese in any food hamper.

images.alt: Irish Ash Serving Board photographed on a plain background

products.title: Cut Crystal Decanter
products.descriptionHtml: Hand cut in Ireland, with a heavy stopper and a base that sits flat. Holds a full bottle. It is the decanter from our Collector Reserve box, sold on its own.

images.alt: Cut Crystal Decanter photographed on a plain background

products.title: Crystal Champagne Flute Pair
products.descriptionHtml: Two crystal flutes with a fine rim and a long stem. They are the glasses in The Toast, sold separately for anyone who already has the Champagne.

images.alt: Crystal Champagne Flute Pair photographed on a plain background

products.title: Beeswax Dinner Candles, Set of Six
products.descriptionHtml: Rolled from Irish beeswax, twenty five centimetres, and they burn for about six hours each. They smell faintly of honey and they do not drip.

images.alt: Beeswax Dinner Candles, Set of Six photographed on a plain background

products.title: Hedgerow Travel Candle
products.descriptionHtml: Ninety grams of soy wax in a tin, scented with blackberry and hawthorn. Burns for around twenty hours. It fits in the corner of any box.

images.alt: Hedgerow Travel Candle photographed on a plain background

products.title: Skelligs Dark Chocolate Buttons
products.descriptionHtml: A bag of dark chocolate buttons from Kerry, meant for baking and eaten straight from the bag instead. One hundred and fifty grams.

images.alt: Skelligs Dark Chocolate Buttons photographed on a plain background

products.title: Killowen Farm Fudge
products.descriptionHtml: Made in Wexford in copper pans, cut by hand, two hundred grams. Contains milk. It goes in nearly every food hamper we build.

images.alt: Killowen Farm Fudge photographed on a plain background
